suites.name: together
suites.description: text.cue is written into package m at #at, as a file of its own beside in.cue, and the package is loaded and looked up at #at. This is a lineage declared in a field of a loaded package, as cmd/thema -p, exemplars and testdata/cases bind it.

suites.name: fill-text
suites.description: package m is loaded without the text, the text is compiled on its own with ctx.CompileString and no file name, and it is filled into the use: use.FillPath(at, text).LookupPath(at). This is how a tool composes separately compiled lineages into one value (#260, authoring.At).

suites.name: fill-text-named
suites.description: As fill-text, but the text is compiled with cue.Filename("text.cue"), as a tool that compiles a lineage from its own file does. #269 found that the file name changes the positions bind reports, never its verdict.

suites.name: fill-use
suites.description: The text is compiled on its own and the use's value at #at is filled into the text's root: text.FillPath(cue.Path{}, use.LookupPath(at)). No caller in the tree does this; #264 records it.

suites.name: unify-use-text
suites.description: The use's value at #at is unified in Go with the text compiled on its own: use.LookupPath(at).Unify(text). No caller in the tree does this; #263's test matrix did.

suites.name: unify-text-use
suites.description: The text compiled on its own is unified in Go with the use's value at #at: text.Unify(use.LookupPath(at)). No caller in the tree does this; #264 records it.

suites.name: third-root
suites.description: The text and the use's value at #at are both filled into field x of a third root: ctx.CompileString("x: _").FillPath(x, text).FillPath(x, use.LookupPath(at)).LookupPath(x). No caller in the tree does this; #264 records it.
